questions.knowledge_point: Writing a Complex Number in Exponential Form
questions.problem: Write the complex number $z=1+2\text{i}$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ giving $\theta $ in radians to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
To write $z$ in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the first quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{2}{1}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2) \\  & ≈1.107.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{5}$ and $\theta =1.107$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{5}\,{\text{e}}^{1.107\,\text{i}}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Writing a Complex Number in Exponential Form
questions.problem: Write the complex number $z=3\sqrt{3}+3\text{i}$ in exponential form.
questions.worked_solution:
To write $z$ in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3\sqrt{3})^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36}=6\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the first quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{3}{3\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=6$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=6\,{\text{e}}^{\pi \text{i}/6}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Writing a Complex Number Shown on an Argand Diagram in Exponential Form
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13973361/assets/f13d134b7dba012b5b71a7a81ab8071b2706586699b8bf21a6df0d5c44c69619.png)

Write the complex number $z$, shown on the Argand diagram above, in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ giving $\theta $ in radians to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =3-\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{1}{3})| \\  & ≈5.961.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{10}$ and $\theta =5.961$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=\sqrt{10}\,{\text{e}}^{5.961\,\text{i}}.
$$

questions.problem: Write the complex number $z=-1+2\text{i}$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ giving $\theta $ in radians to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{2}{-1})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-2)| \\  & ≈2.034.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{5}$ and $\theta =2.034$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{5}\,{\text{e}}^{2.034\,\text{i}}\,.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{3}{2})| \\  & ≈5.3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{13}$ and $\theta =5.3$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=\sqrt{13}\,{\text{e}}^{5.3\,\text{i}}.
